knowledge_point.title: Mapping an Area to a Rectangular Region: Transformations Not Given

question.:question/problem:
Use a change of variables to calculate the area of the finite region $D$ bounded by the following lines.

$$
\begin{aligned}2 x - y&=-3,\qquad 2 x - y=2, \\ x - 2 y&=-3,\qquad x - 2 y=1.\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
**Step 1: Choose coordinates.** Rewrite each boundary using its shared expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}2 x - y&=-3,\qquad 2 x - y=2, \\ x - 2 y&=-3,\qquad x - 2 y=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Choose $u=2 x - y$ and $v=x - 2 y$.

**Step 2: Map the boundaries.** The four boundaries become $u=-3$, $u=2$, $v=-3$, and $v=1$. Therefore

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v):-3\leq u\leq 2,\ -3\leq v\leq 1\}.
$$

![The transformed rectangle.](/tmp/ca9837-templates-z7ii9jxi/17592186129262/rectangle-4c1e7a294f06da50.png)

**Step 3: Compute the forward Jacobian.**

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)}&=\begin{vmatrix}2&-1 \\ 1&-2\end{vmatrix} \\ &=-3\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4: Take the reciprocal and its magnitude.** The inverse is

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=\frac{2 u}{3} - \frac{v}{3}, \\ y&=\frac{u}{3} - \frac{2 v}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant is nonzero, so this linear inverse is defined everywhere. Area uses the absolute value of the reciprocal determinant:

$$
\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|=\left|\frac{1}{-3}\right|=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

**Step 5: Integrate over the rectangle.**

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Area}(D)&=\iint_{\Delta}\frac{1}{3}\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\frac{1}{3}\int_{-3}^{1}\int_{-3}^{2}1\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\frac{1}{3}\cdot\left(2-(-3)\right)\cdot\left(1-(-3)\right) \\ &=\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Use a change of variables to calculate the area of the finite region $D$ in the first quadrant bounded by the following curves and lines.

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=\frac{5}{x},\qquad y=\frac{7}{x}, \\ x&=3 y^{2},\qquad x=4 y^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
**Step 1: Choose coordinates.** Rewrite each boundary using its shared expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}x y&=5,\qquad x y=7, \\ \frac{x}{y^{2}}&=3,\qquad \frac{x}{y^{2}}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Choose $u=x y$ and $v=\frac{x}{y^{2}}$.

**Step 2: Map the boundaries.** The four boundaries become $u=5$, $u=7$, $v=3$, and $v=4$. Therefore

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v):5\leq u\leq 7,\ 3\leq v\leq 4\}.
$$

![The transformed rectangle.](/tmp/ca9837-templates-z7ii9jxi/17592186129262/rectangle-eeb362a486097e36.png)

**Step 3: Compute the forward Jacobian.**

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)}&=\begin{vmatrix}y&x \\ \frac{1}{y^{2}}&- \frac{2 x}{y^{3}}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=- \frac{3 x}{y^{2}} \\ &=- 3 v.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4: Take the reciprocal and its magnitude.** The inverse is

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=u^{\frac{2}{3}} \sqrt[3]{v}, \\ y&=\frac{\sqrt[3]{u}}{\sqrt[3]{v}}.\end{aligned}
$$

These formulas give the unique positive inverse on the whole rectangle. Area uses the absolute value of the reciprocal determinant:

$$
\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|=\left|\frac{1}{- 3 v}\right|=\frac{1}{3 v}.
$$

**Step 5: Integrate over the rectangle.**

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Area}(D)&=\iint_{\Delta}\frac{1}{3 v}\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\int_{3}^{4}\int_{5}^{7}\frac{1}{3 v}\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\frac{2}{3}\left(\ln(4)-\ln(3)\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{3}\ln\left(\frac{4}{3}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

The last step uses the logarithm quotient rule: $\ln(4)-\ln(3)=\ln\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
Use a change of variables to calculate the area of the finite region $D$ bounded by the following lines.

$$
\begin{aligned}2 y&=3 x - 3,\qquad 2 y=3 x - 8, \\ 2 x&=3 y + 2,\qquad 2 x=3 y + 6.\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
**Step 1: Choose coordinates.** Rewrite each boundary using its shared expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}3 x - 2 y&=3,\qquad 3 x - 2 y=8, \\ 2 x - 3 y&=2,\qquad 2 x - 3 y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Choose $u=3 x - 2 y$ and $v=2 x - 3 y$.

**Step 2: Map the boundaries.** The four boundaries become $u=3$, $u=8$, $v=2$, and $v=6$. Therefore

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v):3\leq u\leq 8,\ 2\leq v\leq 6\}.
$$

![The transformed rectangle.](/tmp/ca9837-templates-z7ii9jxi/17592186129262/rectangle-b48a1d910cbfd221.png)

**Step 3: Compute the forward Jacobian.**

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)}&=\begin{vmatrix}3&-2 \\ 2&-3\end{vmatrix} \\ &=-5\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4: Take the reciprocal and its magnitude.** The inverse is

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=\frac{3 u}{5} - \frac{2 v}{5}, \\ y&=\frac{2 u}{5} - \frac{3 v}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant is nonzero, so this linear inverse is defined everywhere. Area uses the absolute value of the reciprocal determinant:

$$
\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|=\left|\frac{1}{-5}\right|=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

**Step 5: Integrate over the rectangle.**

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Area}(D)&=\iint_{\Delta}\frac{1}{5}\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\frac{1}{5}\int_{2}^{6}\int_{3}^{8}1\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\frac{1}{5}\cdot\left(8-(3)\right)\cdot\left(6-(2)\right) \\ &=4.\end{aligned}
$$
